name: Continental Germanic Pantheon
note: Hub collective for the Romano-Germanic deities of the Rhineland and Low Countries attested in votive inscriptions; modeling construct.

name: Matronae
note: The triple mother-goddesses of the Rhineland, attested on >1,000 votive stones (1st-4th c. CE), typically depicted as three seated women; named in numerous cult-epithet groups.

name: Matronae Aufaniae
note: Among the most-attested Matronae groups, centered on Bonn and Nettersheim; numerous inscriptions, esp. 2nd-3rd c. CE.

name: Matronae Vacallinehae
note: Matronae group worshipped chiefly at the large sanctuary of Pesch in the Eifel; ~150 inscriptions there.

name: Matronae Gabiae
note: Matronae group whose name relates to Germanic *geban 'to give'; cf. the Norse Gefjon/Gefn; attested in the Rhineland.

name: Matronae Suleviae / Suleviae
note: Mother/protective goddesses (Suleviae) attested across the Roman provinces incl. the Germanic Rhineland; ambiguously Celtic-Germanic, often grouped with the Matronae.

name: Nehalennia
note: Goddess of seafarers and traders attested by ~160 votive altars at Domburg and Colijnsplaat (Zeeland), shown with dog, basket of fruit, and ship's prow; 2nd-3rd c. CE.

name: Hercules Magusanus
note: Romano-Germanic god of the Batavians, an interpretatio Romana equating a native (Donar-like) hero with Hercules; widely attested in Lower Germany, 1st-3rd c. CE.

name: Baduhenna
note: Frisian goddess named by Tacitus (Annals IV.73) in connection with a sacred grove (lucus Baduhennae) where Roman soldiers were slain in 28 CE; name linked to *badwa 'battle'.

name: Tanfana
note: Goddess of the Marsi whose temple Germanicus destroyed (Tacitus, Annals I.51, 14 CE); a votive inscription also attests her; otherwise obscure.

name: Hludana
note: Goddess attested by five inscriptions from the Lower Rhine/Frisian region; name often linked etymologically to Norse Hlodyn (an epithet of Jord, Thor's mother).

name: Sandraudiga
note: Goddess known from a single votive altar at Zundert (North Brabant); name interpreted as 'she who gives wealth/red sand'; otherwise unknown.

name: Vagdavercustis
note: Germanic goddess attested on altars from the Lower Rhine (notably Cologne-Deutz, dedicated by a Praetorian prefect); name possibly meaning 'martial excellence'.

name: Requalivahanus
note: Male Germanic god attested by votive inscriptions at Pesch in the Eifel; function unknown, name obscure.
